Fit a plot's chrome on the slide around a fixed panel

Source: R/add-plot.R
hv_fit_location.Rd

Anchors the plot's panel to panel_box with hv_ph_location() and checks that the whole figure, panel plus the axis text, axis titles, facet strips and plot titles around it, lies on the slide and below the slide title. If it does not, every text size in the plot's theme is reduced by step (as a fraction of the original size), together with every text margin set in absolute units, until it fits or reaches min_scale. The panel never moves; only the chrome shrinks.

Usage

hv_fit_location(
  plot,
  panel_box,
  slide_width = 13.333,
  slide_height = 7.5,
  title_bottom = 1.38,
  edge = 0.05,
  min_scale = 12/32,
  step = 2/32,
  align = c("panel", "fill"),
  margin = 0.45
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot or patchwork object.

panel_box

Named list list(width, height, left, top), in inches: the slide rectangle for the plot's panel. See hv_panel_box().

slide_width, slide_height

Slide size, in inches. The defaults are the 16:9 HVTI templates.

title_bottom

The lowest point of the slide title, in inches. The figure must start below it. The HVTI title placeholder ends at 1.33 in; the default leaves 0.05 in under it.

edge

Margin kept clear on the left, right and bottom slide edges, in inches.

min_scale

Smallest text scale tried, as a fraction of the plot's own sizes. The default, 12/32, is 12 pt text at the 32 pt PPT base size.

step

Amount the scale drops at each try. The default, 2/32, is 2 pt at the 32 pt PPT base size.

align

"panel" (the default) keeps the panel on panel_box, so every slide puts its panel in the same place. "fill" keeps the panel's height and top but sets its left edge and width from the chrome measured around it, so the whole figure spans the slide with margin clear on each side and sits centered. A plot with short y labels then gets a wider panel instead of a gap on the left; one with long labels keeps about the standard width. Panels no longer line up across slides. Text too wide for the margins (a long title) is stepped down as fit steps down any other overflow.

margin

Space kept clear on the left and right of the figure, in inches, with align = "fill". The default, 0.45, matches the right margin of the standard panel box.

Value

A list with elements

  • plot: the plot, its text sizes and margins scaled by scale;

  • location: the hv_ph_location() result for panel_box, a list width, height, left, top in inches, ready for officer::ph_location();

  • scale: the text scale used, 1 when the plot fit as it was;

  • fits: TRUE when the figure lies inside the slide limits. When it is FALSE, plot and location are those at min_scale.

  • panel_box: the panel rectangle used, panel_box itself unless align = "fill" moved it.

Details

At the PPT themes' 32 pt base size the defaults step the text down 2 pt at a time, to 30, 28, 26 and so on, down to 12 pt.

The figure checked is the placement box plus the actual extent of the title, subtitle and caption text, placed by its hjust (and plot.title.position): a title wider than the slide fails the check even though its cell fits.

Only sizes and margins set in the theme are scaled. The size of text drawn by a geom (geom_text(), geom_label()) is an aesthetic, not part of the theme, and is left alone. For a patchwork, panel_box holds the union of its panels and the whole composition is measured; see hv_ph_location().

See also

hv_add_plot(), which places the result on a slide; hv_panel_box(), hv_ph_location().

Examples

# \donttest{
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(hp, mpg)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Horsepower", y = "Miles per gallon") +
  theme_hv_ppt_dark()
fit <- hv_fit_location(p, hv_panel_box("dark"))
fit$scale
#> [1] 1
fit$location
#> $width
#> [1] 11.52548
#> 
#> $height
#> [1] 5.55918
#> 
#> $left
#> [1] 1.35452
#> 
#> $top
#> [1] 1.85
#> 
# }
